questions.stem: In which four ways may a Bridge Watch Rating be expected to recognise a distress signal?
options: By sight, by smell, by radar and by log entries
By radar, by AIS, by echo sounder and by gyro
By flags, by whistles, by bells and by horns only
By sight, by sound, by radiotelephone and from an aircraft
questions.explanation: TP 10936 lists sight, sound, radiotelephone and aircraft. Radar, AIS and similar instruments may help but are not the four ways listed.

questions.stem: You see a red parachute flare in the distance. What is the first thing you should do?
options: Call the Coast Guard on VHF yourself
Write it in the log and tell the next watch
Report it immediately to the master or officer of the watch
Wait to see if a second flare appears
questions.explanation: A distress signal is reported immediately to the officer or master, who decides on the response. Waiting wastes time, and calling the Coast Guard or logging it is the officer's decision.

questions.stem: On radiotelephone, which pairing of word and meaning is correct?
options: MAYDAY means distress, PAN PAN means safety, SECURITE means urgency
MAYDAY means distress, PAN PAN means urgency, SECURITE means safety
MAYDAY means urgency, PAN PAN means distress, SECURITE means safety
MAYDAY means safety, PAN PAN means urgency, SECURITE means distress
questions.explanation: In descending seriousness: MAYDAY for distress, PAN PAN for urgency and SECURITE for safety. The other combinations swap them.

questions.stem: Which channel is the international VHF channel for distress, urgency, safety and calling, and which channel carries DSC alerts?
options: Channel 16 for voice and channel 70 for DSC
Channel 70 for voice and channel 16 for DSC
Channel 13 for voice and channel 16 for DSC
Channel 9 for voice and channel 22 for DSC
questions.explanation: Channel 16 (156.8 MHz) is the voice distress and calling channel, and DSC alerts use channel 70. Channel 13 is the bridge-to-bridge working channel.

questions.stem: On a foggy night you hear a fog horn that sounds without a break for several minutes. What does the Collision Regulations list this as?
options: A normal fog signal for a vessel at anchor
A manoeuvring signal
A signal that a vessel is aground
A distress signal: a continuous sounding of any fog-signalling apparatus
questions.explanation: A continuous sounding of any fog-signalling apparatus is in the Annex IV list of distress signals. Normal fog signals are made at intervals, so a continuous sound is the clue.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT an Annex IV distress signal?
options: Orange smoke
Flames on the vessel
A single white light on a boat at anchor
Rockets throwing red stars
questions.explanation: A white light on an anchored boat is an anchor light. Red stars, orange smoke and flames on the vessel are distress signals.

questions.stem: A search aircraft is directing your vessel to a casualty. Which sequence of manoeuvres is it using?
options: Fly low in a straight line over the bow and then land
Circle the ship at least once, cross low ahead rocking its wings, then head the way the ship should go
Fly directly away without circling, flashing its lights
Cross astern rocking its wings, then circle once
questions.explanation: The three manoeuvres are to circle at least once, cross ahead low while rocking the wings, then head in the direction the ship is to go. The other options are not the direction signal.

questions.stem: Why do aircraft rock their wings rather than rely on a change of engine tone when directing a ship?
options: Noise aboard the ship may mask engine sound changes
Wing rocking is easier to see on radar
Engine tone changes are forbidden by law
Rocking wings saves fuel
questions.explanation: The Canadian guidance says wing rocking is preferred because of noise aboard ships. The other reasons are not given.

questions.stem: You are heading 090 compass. At 0340 you see a red hand flare at 030 relative. Which first report and compass bearing are best?
options: "Red flare, port bow, 030 relative, just now"; compass bearing 060
"Red flare, starboard bow, 030 relative, just now"; compass bearing 060
"Red flare, ahead, just now"; compass bearing 090
"Red flare, starboard bow, 030 relative, just now"; compass bearing 120
questions.explanation: 030 relative is on the starboard side, so it is the starboard bow. Compass bearing = heading + relative = 090 + 030 = 120. Subtracting would give 060, which is wrong, and "ahead" gives no bearing.

questions.stem: A crew member wants to fire a red hand flare to attract a passing friend on shore. What is wrong with this?
options: It is allowed in daylight only
It is allowed if the master is not on deck
A distress signal must not be used for any other purpose than distress
Nothing, red flares are only a warning
questions.explanation: Annex IV says distress signals are not to be used for any other purpose, and they must not be confused with distress. Time of day or the master's presence does not change that.
